title: Dedicated autoscaler: hard-enforce min/max bounds + emit bound-hit metrics
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description:
Context: Dedicated customers are requesting explicit contractual guardrails on autoscaling to (a) cap spend and (b) ensure a baseline. This PR implements hard min/max enforcement inside the dedicated autoscaler control loop. The key behavior change is that the autoscaler always clamps computed desired replicas to customer-configured bounds (when enabled), and emits metrics/log fields that make the clamp visible (requested_desired vs bounded_desired + reason). This is intended to be deterministic and auditable, and to be safe under conflicting reactive/predictive inputs (prediction work is in a separate PR).

What changed: 1) Clamp desired replicas in the core reconcile loop: desired_raw = max(recommendations) (reactive signals), then desired_bounded = clamp(desired_raw, min_replicas, max_replicas). If bounds are not configured (or feature flag is off), behavior is unchanged. 2) Emit bound-hit metrics: - dedicated.autoscaler.desired_replicas (gauge, value=desired_raw) - dedicated.autoscaler.bounded_desired_replicas (gauge, value=desired_bounded) - dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit_total (counter, labels: bound=min|max, reason=safety|customer_bound, deployment_id, region) - dedicated.autoscaler.bound_saturation (gauge 0/1 when desired_raw > max or desired_raw < min) Also includes structured log fields: scaling_policy_version, desired_raw, desired_bounded, clamp_reason. 3) Add unit + integration tests for edge cases: min > max validation is handled upstream, but autoscaler treats it as invalid and falls back to previous effective policy; max=0 is rejected; clamp behavior for desired_raw below min and above max; cooldown interactions (ensure clamp doesn’t bypass scale-down cooldown); missing policy (nil) is no-op.

Rollout notes: Bound enforcement is gated by account/deployment feature flag (DedicatedAutoscalingBounds). Metrics are emitted regardless of clamp activation, but with clamp_reason=disabled when the feature is off to simplify dashboard wiring.

Risk: The main risk is confusing operators/customers when the platform “wants” to scale but is capped by max. Metrics added here should make this visible and alertable (follow-up alert rules in observability-pack).

Testing: - Unit tests: autoscaler clamp logic, bound-hit counter increments, deterministic reason strings - Integration tests: simulated queue-depth spike, verify desired_raw vs desired_bounded and that fleet provisioning requests never exceed max - Load sim (local): replay of a ramp trace to ensure no oscillation introduced by clamping

Follow-ups: - Predictive signal integration + staleness fallback (ENG-22142) - Console UI surfaces bound-hit state + audit trail (ENG-22144/ENG-22146) - Alerts for max-bound saturation + queue buildup (ENG-22145)

Screenshots: N/A (backend only)

Release note: Internal only; customer-facing docs land with Console/API changes.
commits: autoscaler: emit desired_raw vs desired_bounded gauges + bound_hit_total counter
autoscaler: add structured scaling decision log fields for clamp reason
tests: add clamp edge cases (below min, above max, nil policy, invalid bounds)
chore: metric docs + label cardinality guardrails for deployment_id
review_conversation:
Vanessa Ortiz: Can we ensure this is a hard invariant even if future predictive code proposes something outside bounds? Please add a comment at the clamp site that bounds must be applied last, after arbitration.

Keiko Yamamoto: Added a comment + refactored to make clamp the final step before issuing provisioning requests (decision.go).

Jordan Lee: Two concerns: (1) reason strings should be stable (auditability) and (2) avoid high-cardinality metrics. deployment_id label on counters is probably too hot.

Keiko Yamamoto: (1) Introduced ClampReason enum with fixed values: min_bound, max_bound, disabled, invalid_policy. (2) For bound_hit_total, keeping deployment_id but behind an allowlist gate (only when dedicated.autoscaler.metrics.high_cardinality=true). Default is off; we still log deployment_id in structured logs. Added note to docs/internal/metrics.

Allison Grant: Naming: prefer dedicated.autoscaler.bound_hit_total with labels bound=min|max and clamp_reason=<enum>. Also please add a gauge that can be used in dashboards without counters (e.g., bound_saturation 0/1).

Keiko Yamamoto: Updated per suggestion; added bound_saturation gauge and ensured gauges are emitted every reconcile tick.

Miles Thornton: What happens if policy is temporarily unavailable from control plane? I want no behavior changes and no accidental scale-to-zero.

Keiko Yamamoto: If policy fetch fails or returns nil, we skip clamp and proceed with existing behavior; also added an integration test to assert we never request <1 replicas when deployment is active and min is unset.

Vanessa Ortiz: LGTM once you add a test for desired_raw below min under scale-down cooldown (should still respect cooldown, but bounded result should not violate min).

Keiko Yamamoto: Added test: when cooldown blocks scale-down, desired_bounded remains at current replicas but never below min.

Approvals: Vanessa Ortiz approved; Jordan Lee approved; Allison Grant approved; Miles Thornton approved.
release_notes: Dedicated autoscaler now supports hard min/max replica bounds (feature-flagged).
Emits desired_raw vs desired_bounded metrics and bound-hit counters for observability.
